faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: The questions that come up first — answered straight.
faq.q1: How is SharpTS different from tsc?
faq.a1: tsc type-checks your code and emits JavaScript for an engine like Node to run. SharpTS never produces JavaScript: it type-checks the same TypeScript, then either executes it directly or compiles it to a .NET assembly. There is no Node anywhere in the chain. The setup script uses the .NET SDK when available or installs a self-contained build when it is not.
faq.q2: Why not embed a JavaScript engine like Jint or ClearScript?
faq.a2: Those projects run plain, untyped JavaScript inside a .NET host — a great fit for small embedded scripts. SharpTS runs TypeScript itself, type-checked before execution, and adds what an embedded JS engine can't: ahead-of-time compilation to IL, NuGet packaging, and typed interop in both directions between TypeScript and C#.
faq.a3: Partially. Bare imports resolve through node_modules, and supported module-resolution modes can apply package exports/imports and conditional targets. Packages can still fail when they rely on unsupported syntax, native add-ons, browser globals, or missing runtime APIs. Packages that ship TypeScript source are the strongest fit.
faq.a4: Each mode answers differently. The interpreter is a tree-walker tuned for instant startup — right for scripts and the REPL, not for number crunching. Compiled mode emits IL that the CLR JIT-compiles like any C# assembly, so it runs as native .NET code. In both modes, types are checked up front and then erased — they cost nothing at runtime.
faq.a5: It's a young, MIT-licensed project under active development. The compatibility overview above summarizes common capabilities, measured Conformance publishes the detailed evidence, and STATUS.md tracks implementation gaps.

support.title: What's Supported
support.subtitle: A practical overview of the TypeScript and runtime surface you can use today. For measured detail, explore Conformance.

everydayTypeScript.title: Everyday TypeScript
everydayTypeScript.body: Classes, generics, unions, decorators, modules, async/await, and modern type-system features are supported across SharpTS workflows.

standardRuntime.title: Standard runtime
standardRuntime.body: Common Array, String, collection, Promise, Date, RegExp, JSON, Symbol, and typed-array APIs are available.

packagesNode.title: Packages & Node.js
packagesNode.body: Bare imports and package exports/imports can resolve, but packages still depend on SharpTS-compatible syntax and runtime APIs. TypeScript-source packages are the strongest fit.

knownLimitations.title: Known limitations
knownLimitations.body: Proxy and WeakRef are not implemented. Interpreter and AOT results can also differ on specification edge cases.

features.title: What SharpTS Does
features.subtitle: Write TypeScript that runs on the .NET runtime — interpreted for quick iteration, or compiled to native .NET assemblies.

card1.title: Run it instantly
card1.desc: Point SharpTS at a .ts file and it runs — no build step, no config. Ideal for scripts, automation, and trying ideas in the REPL.

card2.title: Compile to .NET
card2.desc: Ahead-of-time compile to a real .NET assembly — a DLL, a self-contained executable, or a NuGet package — running at native CLR speed.

card3.title: Interop both ways
card3.desc: Call .NET libraries from TypeScript with @DotNetType, and use your compiled TypeScript from C#. Reuse the BCL, NuGet packages, and code you already have.

card4.title: Broad TypeScript support
card4.desc: Use familiar TypeScript — generics, classes, decorators, async, modules, and more — with types checked before your code runs. See the practical compatibility overview below.

card5.title: Fits your .NET build
card5.desc: Drop the SharpTS.Sdk into a .NET project and dotnet build compiles your TypeScript alongside your C# — same toolchain, same output.

card6.title: Editor support
card6.desc: A language server brings autocomplete, type checking, and go-to-definition to VS Code and Visual Studio.

gettingStarted.title: Get Started
gettingStarted.subtitle: Up and running in three steps

step1.title: Install
step1.desc: Run the setup script to install the best SharpTS build for this machine

step3.title: Run
step3.desc: Interpret directly or compile to a .NET assembly

gettingStarted.runCode:
# Interpret (instant startup)
sharpts hello.ts

# Compile to .NET assembly
sharpts --compile hello.ts -o hello

playground.introComment:
// Welcome to the SharpTS Playground!
// Write TypeScript and click Run (or Ctrl+Enter)
playground.requestFailed: The playground request failed. Please try again.
playground.invalidResponse: The playground received an invalid server response.
playground.timingPhaseTokenizeDescription: Turns the source text into tokens.
playground.timingPhaseParseDescription: Builds the program structure from the tokens.
playground.timingPhaseValidateModulesDescription: Rejects module syntax that single-source execution cannot load.
playground.timingPhaseTypeCheckDescription: Checks TypeScript types and reports static errors.
playground.timingPhasePrepareInterpreterDescription: Creates the runtime environment and resolves variables.
playground.timingPhaseCompileDescription: Emits the in-memory .NET assembly after analysis.
playground.timingPhaseAnalyzeDeadCodeDescription: Finds unreachable code before IL generation.
playground.timingPhaseInitializeCompilerDescription: Creates the IL compiler and output assembly.
playground.timingPhasePrepareCompilationDescription: Initializes compiler state for the analyzed program.
playground.timingPhaseEmitRuntimeTypesDescription: Emits helper types required by the SharpTS runtime.
playground.timingPhaseAnalyzeClosuresDescription: Determines captured variables and closure layouts.
playground.timingPhaseDefineProgramStructureDescrip: Defines generated modules, classes, and program containers.
playground.timingPhaseAnalyzeModuleBindingsDescript: Resolves bindings used by generated module code.
playground.timingPhaseDefineDeclarationsDescription: Defines fields, methods, and other emitted declarations.
playground.timingPhaseCollectFunctionsDescription: Registers functions that require generated methods.
playground.timingPhaseEmitFunctionBodiesDescription: Generates IL for standalone and nested functions.
playground.timingPhaseEmitMethodBodiesDescription: Generates IL for class and object methods.
playground.timingPhaseSerializeAssemblyDescription: Writes the generated PE and PDB images to memory.
playground.timingPhaseLoadDescription: Loads the generated assembly and finds its entry point.
playground.timingPhaseExecuteDescription: Invokes your program. Compiled runs can include lazy first-use JIT work.

useCases.title: When SharpTS Fits
useCases.subtitle: Concrete situations where TypeScript on .NET beats reaching for Node — or for C#.

case1.title: Scripts and automation for .NET teams
case1.desc: Write build scripts, dev tools, and one-off automation in TypeScript with the whole BCL available — on machines that already have the .NET SDK and no Node toolchain. No package.json, no build step: point sharpts at the file.

case2.title: Ship TypeScript logic as a .NET library
case2.desc: Compile a TypeScript module to a real assembly and publish it as a versioned NuGet package. With a reference assembly, C# callers instantiate your classes and call your methods fully typed.

case3.title: TypeScript developers in a .NET codebase
case3.desc: Let TypeScript-first teammates contribute in the language they know best. With SharpTS.Sdk, their .ts files build inside the same dotnet build as the C# projects around them — one toolchain, one CI pipeline.

case4.title: Self-contained command-line tools
case4.desc: Compile to a single self-contained executable that runs without a separate runtime install — no Node on the target machine, no node_modules folder shipped next to your tool.
